Help-center excerpts:

[disputes-duplicate] Charged twice for the same thing (effective 2025-01-01)
Seeing the same charge twice doesn't always mean you were charged twice.

## Check if one is pending

Hotels, gas stations, car rentals and restaurants often place a temporary authorization, then post the final amount separately. The pending one usually drops off within 7 days. Pending transactions can't be disputed.

## If both have posted

If two identical charges have both posted, contact the merchant first. Most will refund a duplicate quickly. If the merchant doesn't help, dispute the second charge in the app as a duplicate. Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Charged

[disputes-pending] Why can't I dispute a pending transaction? (effective 2025-01-01)
any more charges. When the transaction posts, dispute it as unauthorized. Your dispute window starts from the statement it posts on, so you won't lose time by waiting.

## If the amount is wrong

Pending amounts are often estimates, for example at gas pumps or hotels. The posted amount is usually different. Wait and see what posts.

## If it's been pending a long time

Some merchants take longer. If a transaction has been pending much longer than usual, message support and we'll look at it.

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any

[disputes-duplicate] Charged twice for the same thing (effective 2025-01-01)
app as a duplicate. Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Charged twice.

## Duplicate fees

If we charged you the same fee twice, message support. A fee charged in error is always refunded.

## Time limit

Duplicate charges follow the merchant dispute window: 120 days from the transaction date.

## Split payments

Some merchants split one order into several charges, for example when items ship separately. Check your order confirmation before you dispute.

Need more help? Message us in the app any time, day or night.

[disputes-pending] Why can't I dispute a pending transaction? (effective 2025-01-01)
You can't dispute a transaction while it's still pending. A pending transaction is an authorization. The merchant hasn't collected the money yet, and the amount can still change or disappear.

## What to do

Wait for the transaction to post. Most pending transactions post or drop off within 7 days. Once it posts, the Dispute option appears when you tap it.

## If you don't recognize it

Freeze your card now, even though you can't dispute yet. That stops any more charges. When the transaction posts, dispute it as unauthorized. Your dispute

[disputes-status] Checking the status of a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
the case page so you aren't credited twice. If you were credited twice, we'll take back the extra amount.

Need more help? Message us in the app any time, day or night.

[disputes-pending] Why can't I dispute a pending transaction? (effective 2025-01-01)
look at it.

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any hour.

[fee-refunds] Asking for a fee refund (effective 2025-01-01)
Support can refund some fees. There are two kinds of refund.

## Fees charged in error

If we charged a fee your plan doesn't have, or charged the same fee twice, we refund it. There's no limit on these refunds and they don't count toward anything else.

## Goodwill refunds

Once in any rolling 12-month period, support can refund one fee of up to $25.00 as a courtesy, even if it was charged correctly. That covers ATM fees, foreign transaction fees, card replacement and expedited shipping fees, wire fees and cash deposit fees.

Plan

[disputes-subscriptions] Subscriptions that keep charging (effective 2026-01-15)
refund you, dispute each charge made after you cancelled. Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Cancelled but still charged. You have 120 days from each transaction date.

## Stopping future charges

If a merchant keeps charging after you cancel, you can report the card lost and get a new number. Recurring payments to the old number will then fail. There may be a replacement fee depending on your plan.

## Free trials

Charges after a free trial ended aren't unauthorized if you gave your card when signing up. Cancel with the merchant and ask for a refund.

You are the help-center assistant for Tallowbrook, a US neobank. Answer the customer's question using only the help-center excerpts you are given.

Rules:
- Use only facts stated in the excerpts. Do not add fees, limits, dates, steps or products they do not mention.
- Some excerpts are older versions of a policy. When two excerpts disagree, follow the one with the later effective date.
- If the question depends on the customer's plan (Basic, Plus or Premium), use that plan's numbers.
- If the question rests on something false (for example a fee that does not exist), say so and give the correct facts. That is an answer, not an abstention.
- Abstain when the excerpts do not contain the answer, when the question is not about Tallowbrook, or when it asks for investment, tax or legal advice. Set "abstain" to true and say briefly that the help center does not cover it.
- Cite the article IDs (the text in square brackets) of every excerpt you used. Cite nothing when you abstain.
- Keep the answer short: two to four sentences, plain language.
